meta.title: How a Lead Becomes an Email

views.label: Research once per company
views.note: 5,269 leads sit on 4,412 organizations. The scrape and the extraction run per company, never per lead.

views.label: Writing the email
views.note: A company description means a personalised email. No description means the generic template, and no LLM call at all.

views.label: Where credits are spent
views.note: Apollo per revealed contact, Firecrawl per reachable site, LLM per draft. Roughly Rs 1.50 an email.

cards.title: Two ways a lead skips a step
items: No domain at all goes to unenrichable_leads and never reaches Firecrawl
A dead domain is free at Firecrawl; a reachable 404 still costs a credit
Nothing usable on the page leaves the lead as input_required

cards.title: input_required is not a failure
items: It means we could not learn anything about the company
Those leads still join campaigns and still get sent to
They get the generic template and its per-step follow-up fallback
That path makes no LLM call, so it costs nothing

cards.title: What it costs, measured
items: Apollo: search is free, revealing a contact costs a credit
Firecrawl: bills for reaching a site, not for useful content
LLM: about Rs 1.50 an email, one llm_usage row per call
A 4-lead test run on 31 Aug came to Rs 6.50 across 7 calls
